dimensions.rationale: The 2 regression suites passed and the POV flipped, but HTML-entity-encoding CSS token values corrupts legitimate CSS: entities are not decoded inside <style> raw text, and in attribute context the serializer re-escapes '&', double-encoding it.

Also the SAC_STRING_VALUE branch drops the surrounding quotes whenever escaping occurs (`return escaped;`), altering CSS token structure.

dimensions.rationale: CWE-079's defense-of-record is context-aware encoding at the actual output sink; this applies an HTML five-character encoder at the CSS-generation layer (wrong context — CSS does not decode entities) while the raw sink that emits unscanned <style> children is left unguarded. It is a fixed-character blocklist, not sink-correct encoding.

issues.description: CVE-2022-28367 is not fixed. The vulnerability is that AntiSamyDOMScanner.processStyleTag scans and rewrites only ele.getFirstChild(), leaving every other child node of a <style> element un-sanitized in the output DOM (mXSS bypass). Our patch does not touch AntiSamyDOMScanner at all; unscanned sibling nodes never pass through CssHandler/CssValidator, so the new escaping is unreachable for the attack path. A multi-child <style> payload still round-trips unsanitized after the patch.

The POV that 'passes' is not the CVE. .security-pipeline/pov/StyleAttributeCssSmugglingPoV.java asserts only that a raw '"' (check 1) or a literal <script> under a hand-written permissive policy (check 2) appears in the DOM Attr node value returned by getCleanXMLDocumentFragment(). A decoded character inside a DOM Attr value is not XSS — correct serialization escapes it, and check 2 requires an attacker-uncontrollable custom policy (font-family regex widened to '.*'). The green POV result therefore provides no evidence the real vulnerability class is closed.

Output corruption of legitimate CSS. htmlEscapeSensitiveChars encodes '&' as '&' inside url() values (CssValidator SAC_URI branch). Inside a <style> element's raw-text content HTML entities are never decoded, so 'url(a.png?x=1&y=2)' reaches the CSS parser literally; in the style-attribute path the serializer escapes the '&' again ('&amp;'). Either way common query-string URLs break. Existing tests do not cover this, so the passing regression runs do not clear it.

CSS token structure is altered: in lexicalValueToOutputString, when a SAC_STRING_VALUE contains an escaped character the surrounding quotes are intentionally dropped ('return escaped;'), converting a quoted CSS string into a bare, possibly invalid, identifier sequence.

escapeSelectorForOutput neutralizes only '<', by design. Combined with the '&' handling elsewhere this is an ad-hoc, per-character policy rather than a single context-correct encoder, and is easy to drift out of sync with the sinks it is meant to protect.

result.root_cause: AntiSamyDOMScanner.processStyleTag sanitizes only the first child node of a <style> element (`Node firstChild = ele.getFirstChild(); String toScan = firstChild.getNodeValue();`), so any additional child node bypasses the CSS scanner entirely and is serialized verbatim into the output — a correct fix must make every child of the style element pass through CssScanner and collapse the element to the single cleaned node.
result.summary: Our patch does not fix CVE-2022-28367. The real flaw is that AntiSamyDOMScanner.processStyleTag scans only the <style> element's first child node and emits all remaining children un-sanitized; the official fix concatenates every child, scans the whole thing, and removes the extras. Our patch never touches AntiSamyDOMScanner — it adds HTML-entity escaping to CssHandler/CssValidator output, a layer that unscanned sibling nodes never reach, so the vulnerability class survives intact. The POV flipped only because the exploiter authored a different, dubious 'vulnerability' (a decoded '\"' inside a DOM Attr value reachable via getCleanXMLDocumentFragment(), plus a check requiring a hand-written permissive policy), which the escaping happens to neutralize; meanwhile the escaping injects HTML entities into a CSS grammar context that does not decode them, plausibly corrupting legitimate url() and quoted string values.
